# Tests that fail INTERMITTENTLY here, one name per line, then the issue that
# owns the fix.
#
# The difference from split-root-known-red-ts.txt is about reliability, not
# about blame.  An entry there must fail on every run or the gate breaks, which
# is what stops that list outliving the bug it names.  An entry here is counted
# only on the runs where it actually fires, so it can neither break the gate by
# going green nor be used to absorb a real regression by staying listed.
#
# Two kinds of entry qualify, and both carry their owning issue:
#
#   #603  host-load flakes, nothing to do with the roots.  Proven rather than
#         assumed: main at fa0ae8b0 failed, the identical commit was rerun with
#         no code change, and it went green.
#
#   #563  the same ambient-instance-root precedence bug as the strict ledger,
#         in a test that only manifests some of the time.  It is here because
#         it is unreliable, not because it is less real.  Removal is still
#         enforced: when #563 lands, the six strict entries all go green and
#         break the gate, and this entry is deleted in that same pull request.
closes attached sockets and exits without waiting for clients to disconnect first #603
renews credentials on the same explicit run and rejects a one-seat binding #563
